title: L¹ approximate identity: ∫⁻|ρ⋆f − f| ≤ ε for all continuous normalized kernels supported in a small ball
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure, and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable. For every ε > 0 there is r > 0 with the following property. Let ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_r(0) (open ball), and let (ρ ⋆ f)(x) := ∫ ρ(t) f(x − t) dt (Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume). Then ∫⁻ ‖(ρ ⋆ f)(x) − f(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(ε), i.e. the [0, ∞]-valued L¹ distance between ρ ⋆ f and f is at most ε.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ), Integrable f → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ ρ : Euclid n → ℝ, Continuous ρ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ρ z) → ∫ z, ρ z = 1 → support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r → ∫⁻ x, ‖convolution ρ f (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x - f x‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε
